hewing_blade.name: Hewing Blade
hewing_blade.desc: A long blade of bog-iron, ground for clearing gorse off the fold walls. The Bearer's foster-father lent it for the voyage and said to bring it back. The grip is wrapped in his old belt.

maul.name: Post Maul
maul.desc: A round of split oak on an ash haft, bound with two iron rings, for driving fence posts. Hesk carries it from steading to steading and sells it when he is short. The leather on the grip is wrapped over an older wrap.

turf_spade.name: Turf Spade
turf_spade.desc: A peat-spade with a long narrow blade and one side wing, for cutting turf in strips. The ash handle has gone silver. It was wedged under a barrow door on the Kin-Mounds to hold the door up.

ice_auger.name: Ice-Cutter's Auger
ice_auger.desc: A long iron ice-auger with an oak cross-handle, for cutting fishing holes. Used as a spear it does not care much what it goes through. The leather on the shaft is worn through in two places, where two hands held it every winter.

sealer_harpoon.name: Sealer's Harpoon
sealer_harpoon.desc: A barbed bog-iron head on a bone foreshaft and an ash shaft, a coil of rawhide line tied below the head. Sealers wait at a breathing hole for hours to throw it once. The line has been spliced so often that it is mostly splice.

spear.name: Spear
spear.desc: An ash-hafted spear with a leaf head. Keeps the cold at arm's length and a little more.

greatblade.name: Greatblade
greatblade.desc: A two-handed blade as long as a door is tall. Swung, it makes its own weather.

bow.name: Bow
bow.desc: A short yew bow for fowling on the fells. Draws arrows from the quiver.

torch.name: Torch
torch.desc: A brand of birch bark and pitched rag on an ash haft, bound in iron wire. Every boat on the strand carries one for landing after dark. The thong at the butt is for hanging it in the bows, head down, so the rag keeps dry.

feast_cleaver.name: Host's Carving Cleaver
feast_cleaver.desc: A broad black-iron cleaver with a knotwork oak handle and a ring at the butt, for carving at the feast. It goes through the joint and into the board under it. The ring is for hanging it by the high seat, on a nail he drove in himself, crooked.

hedging_bill.name: Hedging Bill
hedging_bill.desc: A long-handled billhook, a hooked black iron blade with a back spike on a hazel haft, the binding rawhide. It cuts a stem two-thirds through so it bends and lives. The haft is rubbed pale in two places, a hand's width apart.
